newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Guerrillas target top Colombian oil development.
newsitem.headline: Guerrillas target top Colombian oil development.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas have halted some work in the sprawling Cusiana and Cupiagua oil fields in Colombia's eastern plains, the state oil company Ecopetrol said on Wednesday.

It said a wave of sabotage attacks on oil infrastructure and the killings of at least two contract workers "have provoked the suspension" of some activity in the fields, jointly operated by Ecopetrol and British Petroleum.

The suspension, which Ecopetrol in a statement called a threat to national interests, came after the National Liberation Army (ELN) issued a statement identifying oil installations and anyone working there as "military targets."

A spokesman for BP said the Cupiagua field, which is still under contruction and due to come on line early next year, was the area most affected by the recent surge in guerrilla activity in eastern Casanare province.

Work on four exploratory wells and construction of two oil conduits in Cupiagua has been paralysed since Friday because contract workers are afraid to work at the site, the spokesman said. But he said production of about 185,000 barrels of crude oil a day in the nearby Cusiana field had not been affected.

The British oil giant, the single largest foreign investor in Colombia, has pledged to invest $600 million in developing Cusiana-Cupiagua this year and says production from the two fields should reach 500,000 barrels per day by next year.

But BP Director General John Browne warned during a visit to Colombia in March that the company could be forced to abandon some of its oil exploration projects in the country because of mounting leftist guerrilla activity.

A similar warning was made in April by Stephen Newton, the head of Occidental Petroleum's local subsidiary, who said the country's security situation had hit a new low as leftist rebels demonstrate an unprecedented ability to attack at will, crippling oil facilities and killing workers.
The ELN, Colombia's second largest guerrilla group, specialises in kidnappings and attacks on oil and coal projects across the country.
